indication.text: Prophylaxis of organ rejection in adult patients receiving a kidney transplant, in combination with basiliximab induction, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids; for use only in EBV seropositive patients

citations.quote: NULOJIX® (belatacept) is indicated for prophylaxis of organ rejection in adult patients receiving a kidney transplant. NULOJIX is to be used in combination with basiliximab induction, mycophenolate mofetil, and corticosteroids.
Use NULOJIX only in patients who are EBV seropositive [see *Contraindications (4)* and *Warnings and Precautions (5.1)*].

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) included urinary tract infection (37% vs 36% cyclosporine), diarrhea (39% vs 36%), constipation (33% vs 35%), anemia, pyrexia, and headache (21% vs 18%). Serious risks: increased risk of PTLD (predominantly CNS), other malignancies, serious infections, and PML. Serious infections occurred in 36% of belatacept patients vs 39% cyclosporine by Year 3

detail.text: Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder, other malignancies, and serious infections: increased risk of PTLD predominantly involving the CNS (particularly in EBV-seronegative patients; use only in EBV seropositive patients); increased susceptibility to infection and malignancies from immunosuppression; use in liver transplant patients not recommended due to increased risk of graft loss and death; only physicians experienced in immunosuppressive therapy should prescribe

citations.quote: Increased risk for developing post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder (PTLD), predominantly involving the central nervous system (CNS). Recipients without immunity to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) are at a particularly increased risk; therefore, use in EBV seropositive patients only. Do not use NULOJIX in transplant recipients who are EBV seronegative or with unknown EBV serostatus [see *Contraindications (4)* and *Warnings and Precautions (5.1)*].
Use in liver transplant patients is not recommended due to an increased risk of graft loss and death [see *Warnings and Precautions (5.6)*].
